Voorzetselpaden — B2

Eight hundred and forty-eight frames: business, academic, medical, technical and legal register. Roadmap batches 24–32.

This file is the source. Cards are grouped by contrast set: one verb with its different prepositions side by side, and under each preposition its own examples.

212 verb-prepositions848 cardsframes #2277–#3124

Contrast sets

One verb, several prepositions. The pair is what teaches, so the two drawings must differ on one visible point.

verdedigen tegen

#2277

not drawn yet

verdedigen tegen

to defend against

keep

Scene
A woman standing in front of an easel that holds a small model of a building, her back to it, both arms spread wide to shield it, chin up. Facing her, three people seated at a long table lean forward, each stabbing a finger towards the model, one half out of his chair. The spread arms against the three pointing fingers are the clearest mark.
Must read
one person shielding her own work from several attackers at once.
Avoid
a physical fight; a shop; a blank panel held like a shield.
Pair / note
Single. Academic. The panel is held, not leaning on anything; same camera as zich-beroepen-op-het-verdrag and zich-verweren-tegen-de-eis.
Example
Zij verdedigt haar ontwerp tegen de kritiek.
She defends her design against the criticism.
Build
Zij verdedigt haar ontwerp tegen de kritiek
Build
Hij verdedigt zijn ontwerp tegen de kritiek
Check question
Beschermt de vrouw de maquette met haar armen? Ja
Alt text
Een vrouw staat met gespreide armen voor een maquette terwijl drie mensen aan een tafel er met hun vinger naar wijzen.

#2278

not drawn yet

verdedigen tegen

to defend against

Scene
A football goal seen from the side: the keeper crouches on the line, both arms wide and knees bent, eyes fixed forward. Two attackers in the other kit run in from the right, one with the ball at his feet and one with a leg swinging back to shoot. The keeper's wide arms in front of the open goal are the clearest mark.
Must read
one person standing between a goal and the people attacking it.
Avoid
a keeper catching a ball; a fight; a wall (muur) with no people.
Pair / note
Concrete and sporting. The attack is the thing the keeper stands against; a sport scene, not a legal one like the siblings.
Example
De keeper verdedigt het doel tegen de aanvallers.
The keeper defends the goal against the attackers.
Build
De keeper verdedigt het doel tegen de aanvallers
Build
Wij verdedigen het doel tegen de aanvallers
Check question
Staat de keeper voor het doel? Ja
Alt text
De keeper staat met gespreide armen voor het doel terwijl twee aanvallers op hem af komen.

#2279

not drawn yet

verdedigen tegen

to defend against

Scene
A pavement: a mother stands planted with her feet apart, one arm out in front of her like a bar, the other arm holding her small son behind her leg. A large dog pulls at its lead from the left, teeth bared and front paws off the ground, the owner leaning back on the lead. The boy peers out from behind her knee. The arm held out between the dog and the child is the clearest mark.
Must read
someone putting herself between a child and a threat.
Avoid
a dog being petted; the mother running away; a child alone (zich verdedigen tegen).
Pair / note
Single. A body-to-body defence of another person; the sibling cards defend a goal and a garden.
Example
Zij verdedigt haar zoontje tegen de grote hond.
She defends her little son against the big dog.
Build
Zij verdedigt haar zoontje tegen de grote hond
Build
Wij verdedigen ons zoontje tegen de grote hond
Check question
Staat het jongetje achter zijn moeder? Ja
Alt text
Een moeder houdt haar arm voor haar zoontje terwijl een grote hond aan de lijn trekt.

verdedigen tegen

Scene
A vegetable patch with neat rows of leafy plants: a man in boots stands in the middle with a rake held crosswise in both hands, chin forward. Three rabbits sit at the edge of the patch, one already nibbling a leaf, one standing up on its hind legs. A low fence runs behind him. The rake held crosswise in front of the plants is the clearest mark.
Must read
someone guarding plants against animals coming at them.
Avoid
a man harvesting; a scarecrow; a fence closed with a gate.
Pair / note
A light, slightly comic example to show tegen is the thing attacked or kept off. Concrete and not formal.
Example
Hij verdedigt zijn groentetuin tegen de konijnen.
He defends his vegetable garden against the rabbits.

#2281

not drawn yet

verdedigen voor

to defend before

drop

Scene
A young man standing alone in the middle of a bare hall, a thick bound book held up in his left hand, his right hand open and raised in mid-explanation. Three people in gowns sit in a row behind a long table on a low platform, all looking at him; one rests her chin on her fist. The single standing figure facing the seated row is the clearest mark.
Must read
one candidate standing before a seated panel.
Avoid
a judge's bench; a crowd; a lectern.
Pair / note
The preposition here is spatial. The governed chunk on this page is verdedigen tegen.
Example
Hij verdedigt zijn proefschrift voor de commissie.
He defends his thesis before the committee.
Build
Hij verdedigt zijn proefschrift voor de commissie
Build
Zij verdedigt haar proefschrift voor de commissie
Check question
Zit de jongeman aan de tafel bij de commissie? Nee
Alt text
Een jongeman staat alleen in een zaal met een dik boek in zijn hand tegenover drie mensen in toga achter een lange tafel.
Verdict
Dropped 12 November 2026. The chunk is not a governed verb + preposition: the preposition is free, or wrong, or the phrase is not Dutch. Kept on the page, not taught.

verdedigen voor

Scene
A courtroom: a lawyer in a gown stands facing the bench with one hand raised in mid-argument, a thick file open in the other. Behind her a man sits on the defendant's bench with his hands between his knees. At the bench above, a judge listens with his chin on his hand. The lawyer standing and speaking towards the raised judge is the clearest mark.
Must read
someone speaking in defence of another person in front of a court.
Avoid
a shield; a fight; the lawyer with her back to the judge.
Pair / note
voor here means in front of: de rechtbank is the body that listens and judges.
Example
De advocaat verdedigt haar cliënt voor de rechtbank.
The lawyer defends her client before the court.

one person explaining and defending a plan before a large seated audience.

Scene
A man in a shop doorway leaning back on his heels, left hand flat on his chest, right hand pulling his trouser pocket inside out to show it empty. A shopkeeper in an apron points straight at him with a stiff arm; behind her one gap shows in a full shelf of bottles. The inside-out pocket is the clearest mark.
Must read
the accused answering back, not the accuser.
Avoid
a police officer; handcuffs; a fight.
Pair / note
Answering a charge in public; pair with een-verwijt-maken-aan-de-overheid.
Example
Hij verdedigt zich tegen de beschuldiging.
He defends himself against the accusation.

Most viewers will name the pointing shopkeeper first: beschuldigen van, which is another card on this page. The defence rests on one small pocket.

Scene
A park path: a man in a jacket walks backwards with a shopping bag raised in front of his chest like a shield, one leg lifted. A large goose stands on the path with its neck stretched straight out and wings half open, beak wide. Bread crumbs lie scattered between them. The bag held up between the man and the goose's open beak is the clearest mark.
Must read
a person fending off an animal that attacks him.
Avoid
someone feeding birds; a person fleeing with his back turned (vluchten); a dog (the mother card).
Pair / note
Single. The man protects himself, not someone else: the reflexive zich is the point against the sibling verdedigen tegen.
Example
Hij verdedigt zich met zijn tas tegen de gans.
He defends himself against the goose with his bag.

one person warding off many hostile questions with her own hands and body.

a fan signing autographs; a press conference at a table; running away.

Verbal defence, drawn through the palms. Different from the sibling who is accused: here the pressure comes from many people at once.

a person defending herself with whatever she has against someone coming in.

a woman cleaning; a police officer; a person who has fled out of the room.

#2289

not drawn yet

zich richten op

to focus on

keep

Scene
An archer standing side-on in a field, bow fully drawn, left arm straight, right hand at her cheek, one eye shut. A dog tugs at her trouser leg and a ball bounces past her feet, but her head does not turn. Far off a round target on a tripod holds one arrow in its centre. The straight line from her eye along the arrow to the target is the clearest mark.
Must read
all attention on one goal while distractions are ignored.
Avoid
a gun; a crowd; several targets.
Pair / note
Literal richten op carries the reflexive sense; the ignored dog and ball are what make it zich richten op.
Example
Zij richt zich op het doel.
She focuses on the target.
Build
Zij richt zich op het doel
Build
Hij richt zich op het doel

Kijkt de boogschutter naar de hond? Nee
Alt text

one person giving all his attention to a single task despite distractions.

someone aiming their effort at one group, away from another.

a coach shouting from the side line; an adult match; a coach walking away.

On the right of the line two passers-by have stopped and look at her, one scratching his head. A pen is tucked behind her ear. Must read
a firm position, taken in print.

readable headlines; a lectern; a desk.
Pair / note
The governed form is een standpunt innemen over or tegen.

Verdict
A bare preposition, not a verb chunk. The drawing will be named storm or de boot vaart niet.

Readable as "because of the weather", but it is a synonym of vanwege (203); learners cannot tell from pictures which word goes where.
